# charts/

The IBCS chart set. Every chart is two files: a pure option builder and a
thin component.

## Contract: builders are pure, components are thin

`buildXOption(data, palette, opts) → EChartsCoreOption` takes its colours as
an ARGUMENT and never reads `document`. That is what lets the node vitest
config test it, and what keeps SSR safe. The component resolves the palette
through `ChartFrame` and does nothing else.

A chart shows only figures a service returned. The one arithmetic exception,
documented at its call site, is the waterfall's bar GEOMETRY — the number
printed on the bar is still `step.value`.

## IBCS

`ibcs.ts` is the only file that turns a role into ink: actual solid, prior
light grey, budget outline, forecast hatched. `varianceColor` is the only
source of `--ff-fav` / `--ff-unfav`. A category is never coloured by name —
`WaterfallStep.color` is deliberately ignored for that reason.

`axisDomain` always includes zero. Small multiples share one scale.

## Files
- `chartTypes.ts` — `ChartPalette`, `DEFAULT_PALETTE`, `paletteFromTheme`.
- `escapeHtml.ts` — the escaping EVERY tooltip/label formatter must apply
  before interpolating a ledger-sourced string. ECharts renders a formatter's
  return value as HTML, so an unescaped account name is stored XSS.
- `ibcs.ts` — `roleStyle`, `varianceColor`, `axisDomain`.
- `ChartFrame.tsx` — palette resolution, title, unit note, `unavailable` copy. Optional `summary`: the chart becomes `role="img"` with that `aria-label` (the figures in words; BvA's come from `budgets/tracking/trackingChartSummaries`). Without it the frame renders as before.
- `waterfallOption.ts` / `ProfitWaterfall.tsx` — profit bridge. Below
  `NARROW_WIDTH` the inline value labels are dropped (the tooltip carries the
  figure) and the category labels rotate instead of being hidden. The width
  comes from the live chart — `api.getWidth()` in `renderItem`, and an ECharts
  `media` rule for the axis — so no caller has to measure anything.
- `sankeyOption.ts` / `CashFlowSankey.tsx` — cash flows. `canRenderSankey`
  refuses two cases: a negative opening or closing balance (a sankey link
  cannot be negative), and a period with no non-zero link at all (an empty
  panel under a caption reads as a broken chart). The component picks the
  copy that matches which one it is.
- `bulletOption.ts` / `BudgetBulletRow.tsx` — budget bullets. Polarity from
  the service's favourably-signed `variance`, never from bar length. The
  variance label is set per DATA ITEM on the longer bar (so it starts past
  both bars) with a string colour: ECharts never honoured a label `color`
  function, so the polarity was never painted until 2026-10-29. The grid's
  right margin holds the widest label; below `NARROW_WIDTH` the value axis has
  two splits at 10 px in the compact form (R 1.0M) with `hideOverlap`, names
  truncate at 110 px, and at a phone's own chart width (≤ 280 px: a 390 px
  screen leaves the chart ~260 px) at 90 px. Painted proof:
  `bulletLegibility.test.ts` (1280 / 390 / 294 / 260 px).
- `smallMultiplesOption.ts` / `SmallMultiples.tsx` — 12 months per account.
- `varianceHeatmapOption.ts` / `VarianceHeatmap.tsx` — Budget vs Actual
  account × month variance (actual − budget). A custom series, because
  `lib/charts/echarts.ts` registers no HeatmapChart. Cell colour is
  `varianceColor` only, opacity ∝ |v| / max|v| (no `visualMap` ramp, which
  would issue green and red outside `varianceColor`); a month with no budget
  is hatched with `roleStyle('forecast')`'s decal and not coloured. Top 15 by
  |window variance| with "show all"; below `NARROW_WIDTH` names truncate at
  124 px (104 px at ≤ 280 px) with the full name in the escaped tooltip, and
  month labels stand vertical; past six months every other one is labelled,
  counted back from the latest so a "*" month stays labelled. All at the
  on-scale 12 px (this file is not on the type-scale census's pack-chart
  allowlist; never hide an off-scale size in a constant). Pinned by the
  painted `varianceHeatmapLegibility.test.ts` (1280 / 390 / 294 / 260 px). `judgedThrough` (the engine's
  `projection.judgedThrough`, the last complete month: min(the projection
  cutoff's month, the month before today's)): every later month (in progress or still to come) is drawn
  neutral, marked "*", "not yet judged" in the tooltip and the unit line, and
  left out of the colour scale. A judged nonzero variance is drawn at no less
  than 0.25 opacity (visible on dark); a judged month exactly on budget is an
  outline in the axis-label ink (the legend: "outline = on budget").
- `cashPositionOption.ts` / `CashPositionChart.tsx` — the executive dashboard
  bar. Colour says one thing: below zero is unfavourable. A non-negative bar
  stays actual ink and is never painted favourable — these are four measures,
  not four variances, and green on a payables balance would claim good news.
- `RatioTrendChart.tsx` (+ `ratioTrendStub.ts`) — recharts, not ECharts: Financial Analysis's trend lines. The current month is `Oct 2026*` on the axis and "(to date)" in the tooltip; `RIGHT_MARGIN` leaves room for the last label because recharts measures ticks in the BODY's font, not the painted DM Sans. Proved in Chromium by `tests/unit/print/ratioTrendTicks.test.ts` (2026-10-07).
